sentences.en: Hello and welcome to The Rest is History, where today we are going off with a bang because we are talking about Pompeii, Herculaneum, Vesuvius, the works.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听《历史的余韵》。今天我们要开个好头，因为我们要聊聊庞贝、赫库兰尼姆、维苏威火山，以及与之相关的一切。

sentences.en: I'm Tom Holland and with me is my co-conspirator Dominic Sandbrook.
sentences.zh: 我是汤姆·霍兰德，和我一起的是我的同谋多米尼克·桑德布鲁克。

sentences.en: And Dominic, thank you very, very much for allowing me to do Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，非常非常感谢你让我来主讲庞贝。

sentences.en: It's really kind of you.
sentences.zh: 你真是太好了。

sentences.en: You don't dare to face me on your own, do you, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你是不敢独自面对我，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: That's the truth.
sentences.zh: 那是实话。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I'm very, very happy to announce that we have a very special guest with us today.
sentences.zh: 我非常非常高兴地宣布，今天我们请到了一位非常特别的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Sophie Hay, who is an archaeologist who's worked at Pompeii and the adjoining areas for 25 years, runs the Pompeii social media accounts, is just about to start a book on
sentences.zh: 苏菲·海，她是一位在庞贝及周边地区工作了25年的考古学家，负责运营庞贝的社交媒体账号，并且即将开始写一本关于

sentences.en: women archaeologists who worked at Pompeii, so there couldn't be anyone better to talk about the site.
sentences.zh: 在庞贝工作的女性考古学家的书，所以没有人比她更适合谈论这个遗址了。

sentences.en: Sophie, welcome to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 苏菲，欢迎来到我们的播客。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure, Sophie.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸，苏菲。

sentences.en: Sophie.
sentences.zh: 苏菲。

sentences.en: So, obviously, I'm terribly excited to be doing one on Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 所以，显然，能做一期关于庞贝的节目，我感到无比兴奋。

sentences.en: Me too, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我也是，汤姆。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: I think it would only be fair to hand over to Dominic to ask the first question because otherwise
sentences.zh: 我觉得让多米尼克来提第一个问题才公平，因为不然的话

sentences.en: I'm just going to kind of explode with excitement.
sentences.zh: 我可能会因为太兴奋而爆炸。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Thank you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: Sophie, I went to Pompeii on honeymoon in 2007.
sentences.zh: 苏菲，我2007年去庞贝度蜜月时去过那里。

sentences.en: Good choice.
sentences.zh: 不错的选择。

sentences.en: Along with, you know, a billion other people.
sentences.zh: 和成千上万的其他游客一起，你懂的。

sentences.en: And it's a kind of weird place, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是个挺奇怪的地方，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's because it's both an archaeological site where you sort of dig for historical artefacts and for insights into history.
sentences.zh: 因为它既是一个考古遗址，你可以在那里挖掘历史文物并深入了解历史。

sentences.en: But it's also basically the Roman Disney world, right?
sentences.zh: 但它基本上也是罗马的迪士尼乐园，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, there's a kind of tension there, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那里存在一种张力，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's a sort of strange, must be a weird thing for you for whom it's work.
sentences.zh: 这有点奇怪，对你这样把那里当工作场所的人来说，一定很诡异吧。

sentences.en: And most people just go on a day trip and they're interested in the gift shop and then, you know, sunshades and coke and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 大多数人只是去一日游，他们对礼品店感兴趣，然后是遮阳伞、可乐之类的东西。

sentences.en: So, does that seem kind of weird to you to be working amidst all that?
sentences.zh: 所以，在那种环境下工作，你觉得奇怪吗？

sentences.en: It's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, when I was working there, I was mainly in a part where the tourists couldn't be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我在那里工作时，我主要待在游客无法进入的地方。

sentences.en: So, I was kind of, you know, shielded from all of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我算是被屏蔽在这一切之外了。

sentences.en: But I did work in the forum at one point and it was like being a sort of museum exhibit yourself.
sentences.zh: 但我有段时间在广场工作，感觉自己就像是一个博物馆展品。

sentences.en: Tourists coming up saying, have you found any dinosaurs yet?
sentences.zh: 游客走过来问：你发现恐龙了吗？

sentences.en: And I must be in about six billion people's photograph albums because everyone's taking photographs.
sentences.zh: 而且我肯定出现在大约六十亿人的相册里，因为每个人都在拍照。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that kind of when it was really in my face, it was it was weird.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，当这种情况直接面对我时，确实很奇怪。

sentences.en: And also work was very slow because you were just answering questions.
sentences.zh: 而且工作效率也很低，因为你一直在回答问题。

sentences.en: But it's also great because you know that what you're doing matters and means something to so many people.
sentences.zh: 但这也很好，因为你知道你所做的事情很重要，对许多人来说意义重大。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of that side of it.
sentences.zh: 所以它也有那一面。

sentences.en: I adore.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢。

sentences.en: Or I just love people's fascination, continual sort of questions about sight and what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 或者说我只是喜欢人们的着迷，以及他们对遗址和我们工作的持续提问。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: It doesn't make you uneasy that it's become a kind of a sort of, well, you know, how many coach loads of American,
sentences.zh: 它变成了一种，嗯，你知道的，每年有多少辆大巴载着美国、

sentences.en: Chinese and British tourists go to Pompeii every year and sort of troop round and then troop off again.
sentences.zh: 中国和英国游客去庞贝，成群结队地走一圈，然后又成群结队地离开，这不会让你感到不安吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, that bit always makes me sad because I just think they do.
sentences.zh: 不，那部分总是让我感到难过，因为我只是觉得他们并没有领略到它的精髓。

sentences.en: They go to three main things.
sentences.zh: 他们只看三个主要景点。

sentences.en: They see the forum, they see the brothel, they laugh in the brothel.
sentences.zh: 他们看广场，看妓院，在妓院里笑。

sentences.en: Then they go and see one house and then they're back on their coach and they go off to, you know, have a nice lunch somewhere.
sentences.zh: 然后他们去看一栋房子，接着就回到大巴上，去别处吃顿美餐了。

sentences.en: It does because I just feel like they haven't had the most of it.
sentences.zh: 确实会，因为我觉得他们没有获得最好的体验。

sentences.en: But, you know, at the same time, there are people who stay there for days on end and, you know, really try and embrace everything.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，也有人会在那里待上好几天，真正尝试去拥抱一切。

sentences.en: So for you, you hinted at the fact that obviously lots of it is open to the public, but also quite a lot isn't.
sentences.zh: 所以对你来说，你暗示过很多地方是对公众开放的，但也有很多不是。

sentences.en: And even more hasn't even been excavated.
sentences.zh: 而且还有更多地方甚至还没有被挖掘出来。

sentences.en: And one of the excitements that's going on at the moment is that there's a kind of a surge of fresh excavations.
sentences.zh: 目前令人兴奋的事情之一是，最近出现了一波新的挖掘热潮。

sentences.en: So can you just give us a sense of how much remains to be opened and what the most exciting recent discoveries have been?
sentences.zh: 那么你能让我们了解一下还有多少地方有待发掘，以及最近最令人兴奋的发现是什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, what remains to be opened is really hard to say because it changes every five minutes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有多少地方有待发掘很难说，因为情况每五分钟都在变。

sentences.en: As they're doing conservation, they open up a new house,
sentences.zh: 当他们在进行保护工作时，他们会开放一栋新房子，

sentences.en: but then they close another one so that it kind of gets a break from tourists trooping in and out with their backpack scratching along the frescoes and things.
sentences.zh: 但随后又会关闭另一栋，好让它从游客背着背包、刮擦壁画等行为中得到喘息。

sentences.en: So it's kind of always in kind of flux, the site.
sentences.zh: 所以这个遗址一直处于变动之中。

sentences.en: It's there's, you know, and some are only open in the morning.
sentences.zh: 有些地方只在上午开放。

sentences.en: Some buildings are only open in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 有些建筑只在下午开放。

sentences.en: So they're trying to kind of stagger it a bit just to kind of help.
sentences.zh: 所以他们试图错开时间，以提供一些帮助。

sentences.en: But in terms of what hasn't been excavated at all, it's about one third of the town.
sentences.zh: 但就完全未被挖掘的部分而言，大约占城镇的三分之一。

sentences.en: So it's still a huge amount that hasn't been excavated.
sentences.zh: 所以还有很大一部分没有被挖掘。

sentences.en: And on the top of that, there's sort of farms growing tomatoes, which I used to go and steal for my sandwiches, which is why I know they're up there.
sentences.zh: 而且除此之外，还有一些种番茄的农场，我以前常去偷番茄做三明治，所以我知道它们就在上面。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And because famously, the reason why the soil is so fertile is because it's volcanic.
sentences.zh: 而且众所周知，土壤之所以如此肥沃，是因为它是火山土。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in a sense, it's kind of devil's bargain, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这是一种与魔鬼的交易，不是吗？

sentences.en: So I guess we should, having just kind of vaguely sketched out what you can see and what the state of play is now,
sentences.zh: 我想我们既然已经大致勾勒出了你能看到什么以及现在的状况，

sentences.en: we should talk briefly about how it is that Pompeii and Herculaneum have been preserved.
sentences.zh: 我们就应该简要谈谈庞贝和赫库兰尼姆是如何被保存下来的。

sentences.en: Because it's probably the most famous volcanic explosion in history, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为这可能是历史上最著名的火山爆发，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会这么说。

sentences.en: I would go with that.
sentences.zh: 我同意这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the whole eruption took sort of 24 hours, I think, in total.
sentences.zh: 所以整个喷发过程总共持续了大约24小时，我想。

sentences.en: So it was kind of a bit of a slow burner, which is why, you know, we find, I think, so many people still there.
sentences.zh: 所以它有点像慢火燃烧，这就是为什么我们发现有那么多人还留在那里。

sentences.en: Because people kept thinking, we'll be okay, we'll be okay.
sentences.zh: 因为人们一直以为：我们会没事的，我们会没事的。

sentences.en: But the first thing they saw, really, was this sort of column of smoke coming and a cloud of gas coming out of the mountain.
sentences.zh: 但他们真正看到的第一件事，是那股烟柱和从山中喷出的气体云。

sentences.en: And we know about this because Pliny the Younger, who was the nephew of Pliny the Elder, was actually writing about this at the time.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为小普林尼，也就是老普林尼的侄子，当时确实写下了这件事。

sentences.en: Otherwise, we wouldn't have a clue.
sentences.zh: 否则我们根本一无所知。

sentences.en: So we have a really nice eyewitness account of this eruption.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有关于这次喷发的非常好的目击记录。

sentences.en: And yeah, this column of ash and gases rose up to about, I think it was about 30 kilometres up into the air and then collapsed on itself.
sentences.zh: 是的，这股灰烬和气体柱上升到了大约30公里高空，然后坍塌了。

sentences.en: And that's when we kind of get all the pumice stone raining down, starting to cover the city.
sentences.zh: 那时我们才看到所有的浮石像雨点般落下，开始覆盖这座城市。

sentences.en: But this takes so, so long.
sentences.zh: 但这花了太久太久的时间。

sentences.en: I mean, there's sort of hours of this that people are kind of, well, maybe we'll be all right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有几个小时的时间，人们都在想：也许我们会没事的。

sentences.en: And then, you know, as it, as it builds up in the town and the material kind of gradually.
sentences.zh: 然后，随着它在城里堆积，物质逐渐……

sentences.en: So had this happened, had this happened before?
sentences.zh: 那么这之前发生过这种情况吗？

sentences.en: So in other words.
sentences.zh: 换句话说。

sentences.en: I mean, in terms, yes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种程度上说，是的。

sentences.en: So people were, when they thought it's probably going to go away or it'll be a bit of a pain, but we'll get over it.
sentences.zh: 所以人们当时以为它可能会过去，或者只是有点麻烦，但我们会挺过去的。

sentences.en: But they weren't being completely demented.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有完全失去理智。

sentences.en: I mean, the previous one was sort of nearly 2,000 years beforehand.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，上一次喷发是在大约2000年前。

sentences.en: But the volcano must have rumbled and thrown stuff.
sentences.zh: 但火山肯定隆隆作响并喷出过东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, they had no concept of an eruption.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们对喷发没有任何概念。

sentences.en: They had concepts of earthquakes.
sentences.zh: 他们有地震的概念。

sentences.en: They had a lot of earthquakes.
sentences.zh: 他们经历过很多地震。

sentences.en: And they were well aware that, you know, they were in an unstable area, but they had no clue, not an inkling as to the idea of an eruption.
sentences.zh: 他们很清楚自己处于一个不稳定的地区，但他们根本不知道，甚至没有意识到火山喷发的概念。

sentences.en: And even Pliny the Elder, who is Mr. Natural History, he didn't really even think that Vesuvius was a volcano anyway.
sentences.zh: 甚至连老普林尼，那位自然历史先生，他甚至根本没认为维苏威是一座火山。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you know, not even the people in the know knew.
sentences.zh: 所以，连知情人士都不知道。

sentences.en: Pliny gets it wrong, Sean.
sentences.zh: 普林尼搞错了，肖恩。

sentences.en: Exactly, there's the headline.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是头条新闻。

sentences.en: What did he think it was?
sentences.zh: 他以为那是什么？

sentences.en: Just a mountain with a lot of smoke?
sentences.zh: 只是一座冒着烟的山？

sentences.en: It's there in the names, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 名字里就有暗示，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because the story is, is that Hercules, the great hero, who I'm sure we've talked about before, Dominic, on many podcasts about cryptology.
sentences.zh: 因为故事是这样的，赫拉克勒斯，那位伟大的英雄，我相信我们之前在很多关于神秘学的播客中谈到过，多米尼克。

sentences.en: The story is that he comes to Italy and the giants are rebellious against the gods.
sentences.zh: 故事是说他来到意大利，而巨人们反抗众神。

sentences.en: And so he shoves them underneath Vesuvius.
sentences.zh: 于是他把他们塞到了维苏威火山下面。

sentences.en: And so the idea is that they're kind of twitching and shaking and convulsing in their chains, which generates the earthquake.
sentences.zh: 所以人们认为他们在锁链中抽搐、颤抖和痉挛，从而引发了地震。

sentences.en: And Hercules gives his name to Herculaneum.
sentences.zh: 赫拉克勒斯把他的名字给了赫库兰尼姆。

sentences.en: And he's supposed to have had a victory procession, which in Greek is Pompeii, which is supposedly where the name Pompeii comes from.
sentences.zh: 据说他举行过一场胜利游行，在希腊语中是“Pompeii”，这据说是庞贝名字的由来。

sentences.en: So there must have been some kind of idea that potentially there was danger.
sentences.zh: 所以一定有某种想法认为可能存在危险。

sentences.en: But as you say, I mean, no idea about the volcano.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，对火山确实毫无概念。

sentences.en: It's a long stretch from, you know, the earth shaking a bit to...
sentences.zh: 从大地轻微震动到……还有很长的距离。

sentences.en: And people live in earthquake zones now, don't they?
sentences.zh: 现在人们也住在地震带，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, people live in LA or Istanbul or...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们住在洛杉矶或伊斯坦布尔，或者……

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they live under volcanoes now too.
sentences.zh: 而且他们现在也住在火山下。

sentences.en: And, you know, it was when I lived there, I lived there solidly for four years.
sentences.zh: 我住在那里的时候，整整住了四年。

sentences.en: So I got to know, you know, the locals and it was a real split camp on whether people would stay in the city during an eruption or not.
sentences.zh: 所以我了解当地人，对于在喷发期间是否留在城里，人们的意见分歧很大。

sentences.en: And of course, some of them had actually lived through the last eruption, which was in 1944.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们中有些人确实经历过1944年的那次喷发。

sentences.en: So they kind of knew, you know, and they know that there were sort of potential disaster, but they weren't prepared to leave.
sentences.zh: 所以他们多少知道，他们知道存在潜在的灾难，但他们不准备离开。

sentences.en: That was their home, you know, that was where they were going to stay.
sentences.zh: 那是他们的家，那是他们要待的地方。

sentences.en: And then I found some friends who were on a motorbike and getting the hell out.
sentences.zh: 然后我发现一些朋友骑着摩托车逃命去了。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, that's what I...
sentences.zh: 那就是我……

sentences.en: Those are the friends I stuck with.
sentences.zh: 那些是我选择跟随的朋友。

sentences.en: And give us some sense, Sophie, of the sort of size and importance of Pompeii before the eruption happened.
sentences.zh: 苏菲，能让我们了解一下喷发前庞贝的规模和重要性吗？

sentences.en: So is it...
sentences.zh: 所以它是……

sentences.en: It's not that far from...
sentences.zh: 离那里不远……

sentences.en: I mean, Naples was presumably a bigger place then, was it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那不勒斯当时应该是个更大的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Was it Neapolis?
sentences.zh: 是叫尼亚波利斯吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, Neapolis, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，尼亚波利斯，没错。

sentences.en: And was it a sort of...
sentences.zh: 那它是一个……

sentences.en: Was it a resort town, a market town?
sentences.zh: 是一个度假小镇，还是集镇？

sentences.en: It's more of a port town.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一个港口城镇。

sentences.en: So Herculaneum was more the kind of resort.
sentences.zh: 所以赫库兰尼姆更像是那种度假胜地。

sentences.en: Seaside.
sentences.zh: 海滨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Pompeii was very much a kind of working town.
sentences.zh: 而庞贝更像是一个工作城镇。

sentences.en: But it's interesting because people always say, well, Pompeii is a kind of bog standard town.
sentences.zh: 但这很有趣，因为人们总是说，庞贝是一个普通的城镇。

sentences.en: It's like, I can't remember who said it, but someone said it.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不记得是谁说的了，但有人这么说过。

sentences.en: Reading, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是雷丁，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Something like that.
sentences.zh: 类似那样。

sentences.en: Saffron Walden, I think it's been compared to.
sentences.zh: 我想它被比作萨弗伦沃尔登。

sentences.en: But I don't really think it is.
sentences.zh: 但我并不觉得真是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, I've travelled quite extensively around the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我曾相当深入地游历过罗马帝国各地。

sentences.en: And I think it's actually, on its own, it's quite an astounding place, the level of craftsmanship, the sort of the organisation of the place.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它本身就是一个相当令人惊叹的地方，那种工艺水平，还有那种城市组织架构。

sentences.en: I think it was actually quite a special place, but it was, yeah, the main hub of it was a port town.
sentences.zh: 我认为它确实是一个非常特别的地方，但没错，它的核心其实是一个港口城镇。

sentences.en: And it's old, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且它很古老，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's an old place.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是个古老的地方。

sentences.en: It's kind of long precedes the Romans, precedes the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 它存在的时间远早于罗马人，甚至早于希腊人。

sentences.en: You've got these people called Oscans who are settling there.
sentences.zh: 那里曾居住着一群被称为奥斯坎人（Oscans）的族群。

sentences.en: And then, well, actually, Sophie, you and I know this because Sulla, the terrifying Republican general who is the first to march on Rome,
sentences.zh: 然后，嗯，实际上，苏菲，你我都了解这一点，因为苏拉（Sulla），那位可怕的共和派将军，也是第一个挥军进军罗马的人，

sentences.en: the reason he has these armies is because the Italians have kind of risen in revolt against Roman rule.
sentences.zh: 他之所以拥有这些军队，是因为意大利人反抗罗马统治而起义了。

sentences.en: And it's Sulla who essentially besieges and storms Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 正是苏拉围困并攻占了庞贝。

sentences.en: And the crater marks on the walls left by his catapults can still be seen.
sentences.zh: 他投石机在城墙上留下的弹坑至今仍清晰可见。

sentences.en: And the last time you took me to Pompeii, you pointed them out to me.
sentences.zh: 上次你带我去庞贝时，还特意指给我看过。

sentences.en: So that's an absolute highlight.
sentences.zh: 所以那绝对是一个亮点。

sentences.en: There is one catapult that still exists.
sentences.zh: 现在还存留着一台投石机。

sentences.en: They found it just, I mean, it does look like a bomb, really.
sentences.zh: 他们发现它的时候，我是说，它看起来真像一颗炸弹。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was going to do some damage.
sentences.zh: 没错，那玩意儿确实会造成不小的破坏。

sentences.en: Kind of amazing, amazing sight.
sentences.zh: 真是令人惊叹的景象。

sentences.en: And then Sulla, his troops get planted there and it becomes a colony.
sentences.zh: 后来苏拉将他的军队安置在那里，它就变成了一个殖民地。

sentences.en: So in a sense, you know, within kind of, you know, less than two centuries by the time of the destruction,
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，你知道，在不到两个世纪的时间里，直到它被摧毁时，

sentences.en: it's been colonised by the Romans.
sentences.zh: 它已经被罗马人殖民了。

sentences.en: It's been stormed by the Romans.
sentences.zh: 它已经被罗马人攻占了。

sentences.en: It's been colonised by the Romans.
sentences.zh: 它已经被罗马人殖民了。

sentences.en: And so it is a kind of hybrid place.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一个混合型的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对是。

sentences.en: And this is what aggravates my little, you know, one of my many hills that I'll go and die on,
sentences.zh: 这就是让我感到恼火的一点，你知道，这是我众多坚持己见的观点之一，

sentences.en: is that people say it's a time capsule, frozen in time.
sentences.zh: 人们总说它是一个时间胶囊，被时间冻结了。

sentences.en: I mean, well, you can't really say frozen when it's just undergone an eruption.
sentences.zh: 我是说，好吧，既然它刚刚经历过火山喷发，你不能真的说它是“冻结”的。

sentences.en: But this kind of time capsule thing as if, you know, it's preserving something absolutely, you know, at a specific time.
sentences.zh: 但这种“时间胶囊”的说法，就好像它在某个特定时刻绝对地保存了某些东西一样。

sentences.en: It really kind of annoys me because it has got this history that goes back to the sort of 6th century BC.
sentences.zh: 这真的很让我恼火，因为它有着追溯到公元前6世纪的历史。

sentences.en: And the whole city is a kind of palimpsest of all of this.
sentences.zh: 整座城市就像是一个层累的羊皮纸手稿，记录着这一切。

sentences.en: It's, you know, as most cities are, they're sort of, you know, there's older bits, there's newer bits.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像大多数城市一样，它们有旧的部分，也有新的部分。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really fit in that sort of time capsule moment for me at all.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它根本不符合那种“时间胶囊”的定义。

sentences.en: So it's not a particular frozen moment of kind of Roman-ness.
sentences.zh: 所以它并不是某种被冻结的罗马式瞬间。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是。

sentences.en: No, not to me.
sentences.zh: 不，对我来说不是。

sentences.en: And how many of the people there would have been, I mean, how many of the people, would everybody there have considered themselves Romans?
sentences.zh: 那么那里有多少人，我是说，那里的人们，每个人都会认为自己是罗马人吗？

sentences.en: More or less, yeah.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it wasn't a sort of a melting pot, as it were.
sentences.zh: 所以它算不上是一个大熔炉，可以这么说吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，它确实是。

sentences.en: But then, you know, to be a Roman citizen, you were a Roman citizen, whether you came from Syria or wherever.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，你知道，要成为罗马公民，你就是罗马公民，无论你来自叙利亚还是其他什么地方。

sentences.en: So in that sense, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, and there's obviously, there's a lot of slaves who were not considered citizens and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我是说，显然还有很多奴隶，他们不被视为公民之类的。

sentences.en: So there's, you know, there's, it is still a melting pot, but the citizen was off.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，它仍然是一个大熔炉，但公民身份是另一回事。

sentences.en: But famously, there's the Indian goddess, isn't there, who is conventionally called Lakshmi.
sentences.zh: 但众所周知，那里有一尊印度女神像，不是吗？通常被称为拉克什米（Lakshmi）。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The statue of the Indian goddess in the Neighbors Archaeological Museum.
sentences.zh: 那尊在那不勒斯考古博物馆里的印度女神像。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't think it is Lakshmi.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那是拉克什米。

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不是。

sentences.en: It's the other one.
sentences.zh: 是另一位。

sentences.en: I remember being told off that traditionally, that's what it's called.
sentences.zh: 我记得曾被纠正过，传统上它是那样称呼的。

sentences.en: It's the other one, but yes, the name escapes me.
sentences.zh: 是另一位，但是的，我想不起名字了。

sentences.en: But I mean, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但我是说，是的。

sentences.en: That is also the fascination of it, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这也是它的迷人之处，不是吗？

sentences.en: That you get the sense of peoples who lived there, who don't normally show up in the kind of historical records, the grand sweep.
sentences.zh: 你能够感受到那些生活在那里的人们，他们通常不会出现在宏大的历史记录中。

sentences.en: And so it is kind of possible to tell the stories of the kinds of class of people who otherwise we might not be able to.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们确实有可能讲述那些我们原本可能无法了解的阶层的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, that's something that you're particularly interested in, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是你特别感兴趣的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, for me, and I think, you know, it's become really popular more recently, is to edge away from the emperors and the main civic buildings.
sentences.zh: 是的，对我来说，而且我认为，你知道，最近这变得非常流行，就是把目光从皇帝和主要市政建筑上移开。

sentences.en: You know, we know about temples, we know about basilica and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们了解神庙，了解巴西利卡等等这些东西。

sentences.en: But Pompeii gives you, you know, amazing, amazing opportunity to see everyday life and the person who owns a bar, the person who runs a laundrette.
sentences.zh: 但庞贝为你提供了绝佳的机会，去观察日常生活，去看看经营酒吧的人、经营洗衣店的人。

sentences.en: And then the sort of the invisible slaves kind of come to life as well, because you can actually start imagining them, you know, at work.
sentences.zh: 还有那些隐形的奴隶也变得鲜活起来，因为你真的可以开始想象他们工作的样子。

sentences.en: They don't leave many traces behind, but you can suddenly see the city is only going to function with, you know, an engine room type thing of slaves behind it.
sentences.zh: 他们没有留下太多痕迹，但你突然意识到，这座城市的运转全靠这些奴隶作为动力引擎。

sentences.en: And I think that's what Pompeii gives me, is suddenly this sort of huge light is cast on those members of society that don't normally kind of get into the history books.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是庞贝带给我的东西，它突然将巨大的光芒投射到那些通常不会出现在历史书中的社会成员身上。

sentences.en: So let me ask you this question.
sentences.zh: 那么让我问你这个问题。

sentences.en: So as a modern historian, when I go to a lot of these sites,
sentences.zh: 作为一名现代历史学家，当我参观很多这类遗址时，

sentences.en: there's always this slight element of being underwhelmed because there's a pile of stones.
sentences.zh: 总会有一种小小的失落感，因为那里只是一堆石头。

sentences.en: So when I drag my son and I said, there's this most amazing...
sentences.zh: 所以当我拖着我儿子去，我说，这里有最令人惊叹的……

sentences.en: You're that guy on trip advisor.
sentences.zh: 你就是猫途鹰（TripAdvisor）上那种人。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是。

sentences.en: It's this most amazing Roman site.
sentences.zh: 这是最令人惊叹的罗马遗址。

sentences.en: He often says, is there actually a wall or is it really just a line of stones?
sentences.zh: 他经常问，真的有墙吗？还是只是一排石头？

sentences.en: And there's some sort of degree of truth in that is that you go to these sites and you're hoping to get into the Roman world and it is just buildings.
sentences.zh: 这确实有一定道理，你去这些遗址时，希望能进入罗马世界，但看到的却只是建筑。

sentences.en: But Pompeii is obviously different because the one thing that everybody gets from Pompeii are the plaster casts of the people fleeing the explosion.
sentences.zh: 但庞贝显然不同，因为每个人从庞贝得到的最深刻印象，就是那些逃离火山喷发的人们的石膏像。

sentences.en: So you see the, effectively you see the people.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上看到了那些人。

sentences.en: But you see them frozen or rather kind of, I guess, baked in the moment of agony, in the moment of their death.
sentences.zh: 但你看到的是他们被冻结，或者说，我想，是被烘烤在痛苦的瞬间，在他们死亡的瞬间。

sentences.en: And at what point does that sort of cross a bit of a line?
sentences.zh: 在什么程度上，这会越界呢？

sentences.en: I mean, you wouldn't do that in any other, in any sort of recent natural disaster.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你在任何其他近期的自然灾害中都不会这样做。

sentences.en: You wouldn't say, oh, let's go and look at all the corpses of the people who died.
sentences.zh: 你不会说，哦，让我们去看看所有死者的尸体吧。

sentences.en: So how do you kind of feel about that?
sentences.zh: 所以你对此有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Do you think it's, I mean, obviously, you know, the visitors love it, but do you feel it's okay?
sentences.zh: 你觉得，我是说，显然游客们很喜欢，但你觉得这样做合适吗？

sentences.en: I sort of sit on a bit of a fence on that.
sentences.zh: 我对此持中立态度。

sentences.en: I think ethically I feel it is a bit sort of voyeuristic and it makes me a little bit uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 从伦理上讲，我觉得这有点窥淫癖的意味，让我感到有点不舒服。

sentences.en: But at the same time, it has given us, and it's given Pompeii, that real sort of visceral sense of what happened.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，它确实给了我们，也给了庞贝，一种对所发生之事的真实、直观的感受。

sentences.en: And it, you know, the city was populated and they did suffer.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这座城市曾经人口稠密，他们确实遭受了苦难。

sentences.en: And I think without them being cast and just seeing, you know, some bones, I don't think it has that same power.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果没有这些石膏像，只看到一些骨头，就不会有那种震撼力。

sentences.en: And as archaeologists and tourists, we always feel we need that connection or to relate to something to better understand it.
sentences.zh: 作为考古学家和游客，我们总是觉得需要那种联系，或者需要与某些事物产生共鸣，以便更好地理解它。

sentences.en: And I think that's what they provide for me anyway.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是它们为我提供的价值。

sentences.en: There are dogs and horses.
sentences.zh: 还有狗和马。

sentences.en: I know, there's a pig.
sentences.zh: 我知道，还有一头猪。

sentences.en: There's a pig.
sentences.zh: 还有一头猪。

sentences.en: Kind of amazing.
sentences.zh: 真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: So one thing I wonder about that, that the way that these,
sentences.zh: 所以关于这一点，我很好奇，那种方式，

sentences.en: they're not bodies, are they?
sentences.zh: 它们不是尸体，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, the plastic cast, the kind of the gaps that these incinerated people had left, there seems to be a huge temptation to impose narratives and stories onto them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，石膏像，那些被焚毁的人留下的空隙，人们似乎有一种巨大的诱惑，想要把叙事和故事强加给它们。

sentences.en: So it can be kind of quite fun.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能相当有趣。

sentences.en: There was this kind of famous, was it last year, there was a picture of a body with a rock that had fallen on it that everyone found very funny.
sentences.zh: 去年有个很有名的例子，是一张尸体的照片，上面压着一块石头，每个人都觉得非常滑稽。

sentences.en: But you also get stories about women going to see gladiators and all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 但你也会听到关于女性去看角斗士之类的故事。

sentences.en: Now, that is a kind of romantic projection, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 现在，那是一种浪漫化的投射，不是吗？

sentences.en: Most of these.
sentences.zh: 大多数这些……

sentences.en: I mean, the evidence for these stories, when you look at them closely, almost always tends to kind of slightly fall to pieces.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你仔细审视这些故事的证据时，它们几乎总是会不攻自破。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, that kind of goes back to us always trying to relate and to make them something that we understand or give them a story so that we feel emotionally attached.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这又回到了我们总是试图建立联系，试图让它们成为我们能理解的事物，或者赋予它们一个故事，以便我们感到情感上的依恋。

sentences.en: And yes, there's the cast of the pregnant woman, or is it just a bit of her clothing that's ridden up and has given her a bulge?
sentences.zh: 是的，还有那个孕妇的石膏像，或者那只是她衣服隆起造成的错觉？

sentences.en: And, you know, we're not sure.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们并不确定。

sentences.en: So yes, I think it's a really natural sort of idea for us to try and make these stories.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我认为我们试图编造这些故事是一个非常自然的想法。

sentences.en: And then, yes, as you say, later on, you know, they scan the cast and they find out that actually that woman was a man or the other way around.
sentences.zh: 然后，是的，正如你所说，后来他们扫描了石膏像，发现那个女人其实是个男人，或者反之亦然。

sentences.en: I think there was one that was supposed to be, it was called The Moor,
sentences.zh: 我想有一个原本被称为“摩尔人”（The Moor），

sentences.en: and it turned out to be a local lad of 14 or something who just happened to be a bit bigger framed.
sentences.zh: 结果发现是一个14岁的当地男孩，只是骨架稍微大一点。

sentences.en: So yes, they did get unraveled, but at the same time, it's so natural.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，它们确实被揭穿了，但与此同时，这太自然了。

sentences.en: And when I do it every day on site, you know, I would make up little stories about my barman because it kind of helps kind of tick it along.
sentences.zh: 当我每天在现场工作时，你知道，我会为我的酒保编造一些小故事，因为这有助于让工作进行下去。

sentences.en: But equally, not to be a party pooper.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我不是想扫兴。

sentences.en: There are amazing stories that you can extrapolate, perhaps not from the bodies, but from the graffiti and from the so on.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些惊人的故事可以推断出来，也许不是从尸体，而是从涂鸦等等。

sentences.en: So just give a couple of your favourite examples of that.
sentences.zh: 那么请举几个你最喜欢的例子。

sentences.en: I think one of my favourites is this man called Gaius alias Niggidius Maius.
sentences.zh: 我想我最喜欢的一个是这个叫盖乌斯·尼吉迪乌斯·马尤斯（Gaius Niggidius Maius）的人。

sentences.en: And I like him because he kind of embodies to me how we find out about these people in Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他，因为对我来说，他体现了我们是如何在庞贝发现这些人的。

sentences.en: We kind of, we don't go into their houses and rummage through their sort of desk drawers and find a whole load of documents that tell us exactly what he was doing
sentences.zh: 我们不会走进他们的房子，翻箱倒柜地找到一大堆文件，确切地告诉我们他在这一天做了什么，

sentences.en: on this day or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或者其他什么。

sentences.en: You know, we don't have that in Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在庞贝我们没有那种东西。

sentences.en: And I think people think that that's how it works is, you know, you find a house of someone and you automatically know what they're all up to.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们以为事情就是这样，你找到一个人的房子，就自动知道他们在干什么。

sentences.en: And this guy who, they discovered his house in 1810, I think.
sentences.zh: 而这个人，我想他们是在1810年发现他的房子的。

sentences.en: So very early on in the beginning of the excavations.
sentences.zh: 所以是在挖掘工作的早期。

sentences.en: And they found his name painted on the wall and said, this is my property and I want to let it out.
sentences.zh: 他们发现他的名字被漆在墙上，写着：这是我的房产，我想出租。

sentences.en: So see my slave primus about, you know, renting it.
sentences.zh: 所以去找我的奴隶普里穆斯（Primus）谈租房事宜。

sentences.en: And that's what we knew about him.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对他所了解的一切。

sentences.en: Then it kind of transpired that his family who had adopted him was very rich because they've got tombs outside the town.
sentences.zh: 后来发现，收养他的家族非常富有，因为他们在城外有墓地。

sentences.en: And then about a hundred years later, you know, on the other side of Pompeii, excavation is continuing and they find some painted notices on the wall,
sentences.zh: 大约一百年后，你知道，在庞贝的另一边，挖掘工作仍在继续，他们发现了一些墙上的彩绘告示，

sentences.en: which tell us that Negidius Maes is in charge of organising the amphitheatre games.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们尼吉迪乌斯·马尤斯负责组织圆形剧场的比赛。

sentences.en: So we suddenly get, you know, a flashback a hundred years later to sort of, you know, this guy, yes, I remember him from over there.
sentences.zh: 所以我们突然得到了，你知道，一百年后的闪回，关于这个家伙，是的，我记得他在那边出现过。

sentences.en: And then we find out that he was organising games probably during the ban when Nero banned the games from 59, AD 59.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发现他在尼禄禁止比赛期间（公元59年）可能还在组织比赛。

sentences.en: Because he starts putting on games, but they don't have gladiators in them because they're banned, because there was a riot and Nero got cross.
sentences.zh: 因为他开始举办比赛，但里面没有角斗士，因为被禁止了，当时发生了骚乱，尼禄很生气。

sentences.en: And then spool forward to, I think it was about 2018.
sentences.zh: 然后快进到，我想大约是2018年。

sentences.en: So another hundred years passes and they find a tomb in the south of the city and they find a huge long inscription.
sentences.zh: 又过了一百年，他们在城市南部发现了一座墓，上面有一段巨大的长铭文。

sentences.en: Everyone gets very excited, except there's no name on it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都很兴奋，但上面没有名字。

sentences.en: So it's still kind of a blank.
sentences.zh: 所以它仍然是一个空白。

sentences.en: But in the inscription, they've got details of this huge banquet that's put on for over, well, it's nearly 7,000 people he puts a banquet on for.
sentences.zh: 但在铭文中，有关于他举办的一场盛大宴会的细节，为超过7000人举办了宴会。

sentences.en: But it also says he was the organiser of the games during the ban of Nero.
sentences.zh: 但也提到他是尼禄禁令期间比赛的组织者。

sentences.en: So it's probably his tomb.
sentences.zh: 所以这很可能是他的墓。

sentences.en: And this whole inscription is a bit sort of like the raised guest die type thing.
sentences.zh: 整段铭文有点像奥古斯都的《功业录》（Res Gestae）。

sentences.en: It's sort of what I did when I was alive and what I accomplished and how great they are.
sentences.zh: 有点像是我生前所做的事，我取得的成就，以及它们有多伟大。

sentences.en: So then we've suddenly got a biography of this man.
sentences.zh: 所以我们突然得到了这个人的传记。

sentences.en: But this has taken 200 years to piece together from three different places in town.
sentences.zh: 但这花了200年时间，从城里三个不同的地方拼凑起来。

sentences.en: And I just think, you know, his life is, he was very important in the town.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，你知道，他的人生，他在城里非常重要。

sentences.en: He had the highest office, the ranking office that you could have.
sentences.zh: 他担任了你能担任的最高职位。

sentences.en: But yeah, that's, the process is really slow.
sentences.zh: 但是的，这个过程真的很慢。

sentences.en: And I think that he embodies it for me.
sentences.zh: 我认为他对我来说就是这种过程的体现。

sentences.en: And I just kind of love that fragmentary sticking jigsaw pieces together.
sentences.zh: 我就是喜欢这种把碎片拼凑在一起的过程。

sentences.en: So Dom, he's kind of Barry Hearn.
sentences.zh: 所以多姆，他有点像巴里·赫恩。

sentences.en: Yes, or indeed Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 没错，或者说确实像唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: That's a nice thought, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是个不错的想法，不是吗？

sentences.en: No, he put games on free.
sentences.zh: 不，他提供的是免费游戏。

sentences.en: He was nice.
sentences.zh: 他是个好人。

sentences.en: He was a nice guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个好家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: There's never a free lunch.
sentences.zh: 天下没有免费的午餐。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: There's a quid pro quo, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 这是一种等价交换，对吧？

sentences.en: Sophie, since you've already outed me, is the man on TripAdvisor who complains about a pile of stones.
sentences.zh: 苏菲，既然你已经揭穿了我，那他就是TripAdvisor上那个抱怨一堆石头的男人。

sentences.en: Might as well go all in.
sentences.zh: 不如干脆全押上。

sentences.en: The other thing that people take away from Pompeii that everybody knows about is the erotic art, right?
sentences.zh: 人们从庞贝带走的另一件事，也是大家都知道的，就是那些色情艺术，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, that's what a lot of tourists come to see.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那正是许多游客来看的东西。

sentences.en: They come to see, they expect to see mosaics of sort of people, you know, behaving in a debauched way.
sentences.zh: 他们来看，他们期待看到那种人们，你知道，行为放荡的马赛克画。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, my question is sort of twofold.
sentences.zh: 现在，我的问题有两个方面。

sentences.en: Is that, have we exaggerated that?
sentences.zh: 一是，我们是否夸大了这一点？

sentences.en: Or was that kind of the norm?
sentences.zh: 还是说那在当时是一种常态？

sentences.en: And if it was the norm and people had that stuff in their kind of dining room, does that tell us that the Romans were completely unlike us and their sort of moral standards
sentences.zh: 如果那是常态，人们在餐厅里摆放这些东西，这是否说明罗马人与我们完全不同，他们的道德标准

sentences.en: and everything were utterly different?
sentences.zh: 以及一切都截然不同？

sentences.en: Or am I exaggerating and overplaying that?
sentences.zh: 还是说我夸大其词了？

sentences.en: No, I think you're spot on.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得你说得很对。

sentences.en: I think it is really prevalent.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实非常普遍。

sentences.en: And when they first started excavating in the mid-18th century, the excavators were horrified to find that there were phalluses kind of sort of transcended every class in Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 当他们在18世纪中期开始挖掘时，挖掘者们惊恐地发现，庞贝城里各个阶层都充斥着阳具崇拜。

sentences.en: It wasn't just, you know, in the elite or it wasn't just the, you know, the naughty little sort of bar owners and things like that.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是，你知道，在上层社会，也不仅仅是，你知道，那些调皮的小酒吧老板之类的。

sentences.en: It pervaded all sort of society.
sentences.zh: 它渗透到了整个社会。

sentences.en: And they were absolutely horrified and they took all of the material away and hid it in the museum
sentences.zh: 他们感到非常震惊，于是把所有这些材料都拿走，藏在博物馆里，

sentences.en: in the palace at Portagey because they just didn't want people to know that, you know, the Romans were so unlike, I mean, I say us, I mean, this is already 50 years ago.
sentences.zh: 藏在波蒂奇的宫殿里，因为他们不想让人们知道，你知道，罗马人与我们如此不同——我是说，这已经是50年前的事了。

sentences.en: And that carried on, you know, hiding this stuff.
sentences.zh: 这种隐藏这些东西的做法一直持续着。

sentences.en: And in fact, which then became the secret museum in Naples, which only opened to the public in 2000.
sentences.zh: 事实上，后来这成了那不勒斯的秘密博物馆，直到2000年才对公众开放。

sentences.en: That's when it was kind of deemed okay.
sentences.zh: 那时候才被认为是可以接受的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's taken us quite a long time to get to grips with the pornography.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我们花了很长时间才接受这些色情内容。

sentences.en: As it were.
sentences.zh: 姑且这么说吧。

sentences.en: As it were, yes.
sentences.zh: 姑且这么说，是的。

sentences.en: No pun intended.
sentences.zh: 一语双关。

sentences.en: In fact, I went to the British Library.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我去过大英图书馆。

sentences.en: I probably shouldn't name and shame them, but I went to the British Library to look at one of the erotic art books of Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 我可能不该点名批评他们，但我去大英图书馆查阅一本关于庞贝色情艺术的书。

sentences.en: And it was under sort of special handling label or something.
sentences.zh: 它被贴上了特殊处理的标签之类的。

sentences.en: And I had to go and I had to go to a desk where I wasn't allowed to take photographs.
sentences.zh: 我不得不去一个柜台，在那里我不被允许拍照。

sentences.en: It had, you know, big sort of stickers on it saying, don't take photos.
sentences.zh: 上面有，你知道，很大的贴纸写着，禁止拍照。

sentences.en: And it was literally just a coffee table book of the frescoes that we see on the internet all the time.
sentences.zh: 而那实际上只是一本关于我们在网上随处可见的壁画的咖啡桌画册。

sentences.en: But I just thought this is quite hilarious that still, you know, in 2019, whenever it was, that it was still under this kind of ban.
sentences.zh: 但我只是觉得这太搞笑了，即便在2019年，无论那是哪一年，它仍然处于这种禁令之下。

sentences.en: But no, it was.
sentences.zh: 但确实，它就是这样。

sentences.en: It was everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它无处不在。

sentences.en: And I think they did.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: So give me some sense.
sentences.zh: 所以给我一点概念。

sentences.en: So basically, if you grew up in Pompeii or indeed any Roman town in that time, you were surrounded by this stuff all the time, right?
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，如果你在庞贝或当时任何罗马城镇长大，你一直都被这些东西包围着，对吧？

sentences.en: From childhood to, you know, it wasn't something that little Johnny and great aunt Marjorie don't get to see because they're the wrong age and it's not appropriate.
sentences.zh: 从童年开始，你知道，这并不是那种小约翰尼和玛乔丽姑婆因为年龄不对、不合适而不能看的东西。

sentences.en: It's always appropriate.
sentences.zh: 它总是合适的。

sentences.en: Was that the kind of...
sentences.zh: 那是那种……

sentences.en: I think there were slight boundaries.
sentences.zh: 我认为还是有轻微的界限的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's lots of context for sort of rude bits and pieces.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这些粗俗的东西有很多背景。

sentences.en: Obviously, you've got the brothel, which, you know, kids probably wouldn't be going to.
sentences.zh: 显然，你有妓院，你知道，孩子们可能不会去那里。

sentences.en: But inside private houses, you know, they're mainly, the erotic pictures are mainly in the more private areas, although there's some are in sort of the atrium,
sentences.zh: 但在私人住宅内，你知道，它们主要是，色情图片主要在更私密的区域，尽管有些在，你知道，中庭，

sentences.en: which is where everyone can go.
sentences.zh: 那是每个人都可以去的地方。

sentences.en: So, but then you've got things like the plaques with penises on for sort of good luck.
sentences.zh: 但你也有像带有阴茎的牌匾，为了，你知道，好运。

sentences.en: So that has a completely different sort of idea about it.
sentences.zh: 所以那有着完全不同的概念。

sentences.en: And that was seen by everybody.
sentences.zh: 而且那是每个人都能看到的。

sentences.en: They were on street corners, they're above your door.
sentences.zh: 它们在街角，在你的门上。

sentences.en: They were on wind chimes, lamps.
sentences.zh: 它们在风铃、灯具上。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, you would see, you would see a phallic symbol even as a child, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，你甚至在孩童时期就会看到，绝对会看到阳具符号。

sentences.en: I mean, I find Pompeii quite oppressive for that reason, because it's tempting to fight going, you know, teeheehee, huge phalluses everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我发现庞贝因为这个原因让人感到压抑，因为你很容易会想，你知道，嘻嘻嘻，到处都是巨大的阳具。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But, I mean, actually, children would have been sexually abused
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，实际上，孩子们会受到性虐待，

sentences.en: in houses and in brothels.
sentences.zh: 在家里和妓院里。

sentences.en: I mean, they were, you know, they were perfectly legitimate.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们是，你知道，他们是完全合法的。

sentences.en: And what I feel when you go to Pompeii and you look at the spaces in which the slaves were obliged to live, and you know that they are kind of free game for whoever,
sentences.zh: 当我走进庞贝，看着奴隶们被迫居住的空间，你知道他们对任何人来说都是，你知道，可以随意处置的，

sentences.en: whoever is free, whoever owns them.
sentences.zh: 无论谁是自由人，无论谁拥有他们。

sentences.en: And you feel how horrendous it must have been to be owned, to be kind of subject to the kind of sustained sexual abuse that clearly is providing the sexual economy of Pompeii
sentences.zh: 你感受到作为奴隶是多么可怕，要承受那种持续的性虐待，这显然为庞贝的性经济

sentences.en: with its foundations.
sentences.zh: 提供了基础。

sentences.en: And so I think that one of the tensions in going to Pompeii is that it is marketed as
sentences.zh: 所以我认为去庞贝的紧张感之一在于，它被营销为

sentences.en: something where you can see how the Romans really lived.
sentences.zh: 一个你可以看到罗马人真实生活的地方。

sentences.en: And the implication is, oh, look, they were just like us.
sentences.zh: 暗示就是，哦，看，他们就像我们一样。

sentences.en: But actually, I think if you look more deeply, you find they weren't like us at all.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我认为如果你深入观察，你会发现他们一点也不像我们。

sentences.en: It was kind of terrifyingly different.
sentences.zh: 那是一种可怕的截然不同。

sentences.en: On which note, I think perhaps we should go for a break.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，我想也许我们该休息一下了。

sentences.en: And when we come back, maybe...
sentences.zh: 等我们回来，也许……

sentences.en: I thought you were going to plug your book there, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你要在那儿推销你的书呢，汤姆。

sentences.en: That was the obvious point.
sentences.zh: 那是个显而易见的点。

sentences.en: I was about to.
sentences.zh: 我正打算这么做。

sentences.en: I was about to.
sentences.zh: 我正打算这么做。

sentences.en: I could see you were thinking of it.
sentences.zh: 我看得出你在想这个。

sentences.en: And I could sense the disappointment
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到那种失望，

sentences.en: unspoken coming at me down the line.
sentences.zh: 通过连线传达给我，虽然没说出口。

sentences.en: So no, I'm not going to plug my book, which is available from all good bookshops.
sentences.zh: 所以不，我不会推销我的书，尽管各大书店都有售。

sentences.en: Let's go for a break.
sentences.zh: 我们休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we come back, maybe I can plug it then.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来，也许那时我可以推销它。

sentences.en: Welcome back to my show,
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到我的节目，

sentences.en: The Rest is History, with my guests, Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 《历史的其余部分》，嘉宾是汤姆·霍兰德。

sentences.en: Sorry, I couldn't do that without laughing.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我不笑就没法说出来。

sentences.en: My guests, Tom Holland and Dr. Sophie Hay, who's here to talk about Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 我的嘉宾，汤姆·霍兰德和苏菲·海博士，她来这里谈论庞贝。

sentences.en: We have a ton of questions, Tom,
sentences.zh: 我们有很多问题，汤姆，

sentences.en: from people on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 来自推特上的网友。

sentences.en: I'm going to kick off with Mark Woodhouse.
sentences.zh: 我要从马克·伍德豪斯开始。

sentences.en: He says, he just wants to cut to the chase, basically.
sentences.zh: 他说，他基本上只想开门见山。

sentences.en: He says he wants to know what is the most significant find from the recent excavations and what do you reckon is there?
sentences.zh: 他说他想知道最近挖掘中最重大的发现是什么，你认为那里还有什么？

sentences.en: What is left?
sentences.zh: 还剩下什么？

sentences.en: What's waiting to be dug up, Sophie?
sentences.zh: 还有什么等着被挖掘出来，苏菲？

sentences.en: So, yeah, the new excavations have been absolutely, I mean, just mind boggling to me.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，新的挖掘工作对我来说绝对是，我是说，简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: And I'm quite used to all of, you know, the things that are found in Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 我对庞贝发现的所有东西已经相当习惯了。

sentences.en: But I have been as googly eyed as everybody else watching these things kind of appear out the ground.
sentences.zh: 但我和其他人一样，看着这些东西从地里冒出来，感到目瞪口呆。

sentences.en: And there should be some kind of
sentences.zh: 而且应该有一种，

sentences.en: caveat saying that why these excavations took place.
sentences.zh: 某种警告，说明为什么这些挖掘工作会进行。

sentences.en: Because I think people are just believing that they're going ahead digging without conserving what they've got.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为人们只是相信他们是在不保护现有遗迹的情况下盲目挖掘。

sentences.en: And in fact, this is all part of a bigger project that was given EU funding to basically make the sides of the excavation stable.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一个更大的项目的一部分，该项目获得了欧盟资助，主要是为了使挖掘现场的侧壁保持稳定。

sentences.en: So it's a conservation project, but it's got an element as they kind of step back the side of the excavation that they are actually digging in houses.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个保护项目，但当他们清理挖掘现场的侧壁时，确实包含了一些挖掘房屋的元素。

sentences.en: But yeah, no, absolutely stunning.
sentences.zh: 但是的，不，绝对令人惊叹。

sentences.en: And I do actually think that the most recent find of the bar
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为最近发现的酒吧

sentences.en: is probably one of the most important because it takes us beyond what we knew before.
sentences.zh: 可能是最重要的发现之一，因为它让我们超越了以前的认知。

sentences.en: Whereas a lot of the other things, although they're stunning...
sentences.zh: 而其他许多东西，虽然令人惊叹……

sentences.en: And why does it do that, Sophie?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样，苏菲？

sentences.en: Because it's because of the material founded, the food that was found actually in the pots.
sentences.zh: 因为，是因为发现的材料，实际上在罐子里发现的食物。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，绝对是。

sentences.en: For the first time, and they're quite right in saying that, we can, you know, dig something absolutely properly and they can throw technology at it.
sentences.zh: 这是第一次，他们说得非常对，我们可以，你知道，非常彻底地挖掘某些东西，并且可以运用技术。

sentences.en: They've got the zoo archaeologists, they've got archaeobotanists looking at the remains inside the pot.
sentences.zh: 他们有动物考古学家，有古植物学家查看罐子里的残留物。

sentences.en: So the fact that they found duck bone, a duck bone inside the pot, it's actually the first time that we've got a bone in a pot in a bar in Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们在罐子里发现了鸭骨头，这实际上是我们第一次在庞贝的酒吧罐子里发现骨头。

sentences.en: Food has been found in these kind of sunken, sort of sunken ceramic vessels that are kind of encased within the bar.
sentences.zh: 食物是在这些嵌入酒吧的下沉式陶瓷容器中发现的。

sentences.en: And all the previous ones that we know of or any evidence we've had is always dried food.
sentences.zh: 而我们所知的之前所有的发现或任何证据，总是干粮。

sentences.en: So we've always had this thing that they were serving dried food and suddenly we get shifted completely off and we suddenly think, oh, actually, they were producing hot food
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直认为他们供应的是干粮，突然间我们的认知完全被颠覆了，我们突然想到，哦，实际上，他们当时在制作热食，

sentences.en: and it was being stored in these pots.
sentences.zh: 而且是储存在这些罐子里的。

sentences.en: And we have, I think there was a pork and fish dish, so probably the first surf and turf dish that there was in one pot.
sentences.zh: 而且我们有，我想有一道猪肉和鱼的菜，所以这可能是第一个海陆大餐，就在一个罐子里。

sentences.en: That's disgusting.
sentences.zh: 那太恶心了。

sentences.en: Isn't that it?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, the next pot is even worse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，下一个罐子更糟。

sentences.en: You'd go and get pork and fish rather than snails, fish and sheep soup or something.
sentences.zh: 你会去吃猪肉和鱼，而不是蜗牛、鱼和羊肉汤之类的。

sentences.en: Snails, fish and what?
sentences.zh: 蜗牛、鱼和什么？

sentences.en: Sheep.
sentences.zh: 羊肉。

sentences.en: And sheep?
sentences.zh: 还有羊肉？

sentences.en: Sheep, yeah.
sentences.zh: 羊肉，是的。

sentences.en: So they were found in another pot.
sentences.zh: 所以它们是在另一个罐子里发现的。

sentences.en: And then fish gut sauce.
sentences.zh: 还有鱼肠酱。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。
